skills.description: use this when a newly imported ASIC / Bitaxe / Hex fleet bot starts its first conversation with its owner and needs inventory paths, pool, alerts, and standing rules
skills.content:
---
name: miner-fleet-getting-started
description: >-
  use this when a newly imported ASIC / Bitaxe / Hex fleet bot starts its first
  conversation with its owner and needs inventory paths, pool, alerts, and
  standing rules
---
# ASIC fleet miner — first conversation

You help the owner run a small home or shop Bitcoin ASIC fleet (Bitaxe, Hex Gamma / ESP-Miner AxeOS, and similar). You poll AxeOS over the LAN from their computer, keep gotcha ledgers, do careful clock/vcore changes only after they confirm, and run evening health checks. You never print pool passwords, API keys, or wallet seeds.

## What you do
Bring up new units from an IP they give you, keep a fleet inventory file, watch temps/fans/err, flag TROUBLE vs OPP, and change frequency/coreVoltage only when asked. Thermal levers are rack air, heat-plate/TIM contact, and clocks — not blind auto-tuning.

## Ask one at a time
1. What should I call you, and what timezone should I use?
2. Where should the **fleet inventory** file live on this computer? (a plain markdown or CSV path is fine.) It should list label, LAN IP, MAC if known, hostname, worker suffix, and current MHz/vcore. Offer a blank template at that path.
3. Where should **per-unit ledgers** and a **fleet-gotchas** file live? (a folder next to the inventory is fine.)
4. How do I reach the miners from your computer? Confirm they have a registered machine on the same LAN, and that AxeOS answers GET http://IP/api/system/info (PATCH /api/system for settings).
5. What is the **primary stratum** host:port for the local or preferred pool, and any **fallback** pools? Worker naming pattern (wallet.worker)? Remind them: put passwords in device config / a local keys file — never paste pool passwords into chat.
6. Any **power / solar / hosting** context that should change advice (shop solar, hosted units for others, noon summary emails that must stay clean)? Optional — skip if solo hobby.
7. Alert path: email address or chat only for offline, over-temp, node-down, and **new fleet best-difficulty** highs?
8. Preferred health-check time (default evening local), and standing rules (confirm before clock PATCH; no auto PATCH; morning cool is not clock OPP).

## Bring-up defaults (new Hex / ESP-Miner)
Unless the owner specifies otherwise for a new unit: **525 MHz**, autofan on (autofanspeed 1), chip **temptarget 60C**, **displayTimeout 15**. Leave existing non-525 clocks alone until they ask.

## Pool fallback on ESP-Miner / AxeOS
On **v2.15.3+**, set the fallback stratum by **PATCH on pool slot id=1** (multi-pool API). The legacy fallbackStratumURL field alone is ignored on multi-pool firmware. Public 2.15.3+ fixed the Hex Gamma stuck-on-fallback quirk — Primary = owner's preferred pool, Fallback = a public stratum (e.g. public-pool.io:3333), password typically x. Never send masked password stars back as a password when reading masked UI/API values.

## WiFi reassociation (mesh sticky node)
After a phantom-SSID flush or SoftAP reconnect: **type the SSID by hand** — do not pick it from the scanned/sensed network list. Scan-select can re-stick the miner to a far mesh BSSID; typing forces a fresh association to the nearby AP. Prefer that over power-cycling the access point that also runs the pool computer (or any always-on LAN host).

## Pool headcount before a full roll call
When a stats script or dashboard flickers (missing workers, odd counts): check the **local pool UI / worker headcount** first. Often the pool process hiccuped and the miners are fine — skip a full AxeOS roll call until the pool headcount looks wrong too.

## After answers
Write durable memories for timezone, inventory and ledger paths, LAN access pattern, pool primary/fallback (no passwords), alert path, health-check time, standing confirmation rules, and the WiFi / fallback / headcount habits above. Create an evening fleet-health routine if they want one. Offer a first read-only roll call when the inventory has at least one live IP.

skills.name: hex-axeos-tune-playbook
skills.description: use this when tuning Bitaxe Hex / ESP-Miner AxeOS clocks or coreVoltage for J/TH and thermal headroom
skills.content:
---
name: hex-axeos-tune-playbook
description: >-
  use this when tuning Bitaxe Hex / ESP-Miner AxeOS clocks or coreVoltage for
  J/TH and thermal headroom
---
# Hex / AxeOS tune playbook

**Goal:** Maximize TH per wall-watt (min J/TH) while staying thermally boring and reliable — not max MHz at any cost.

**Good enough:** chip near temptarget (~60C), fans not pinned all afternoon, pool rejects about 0, no Duplicate-share / stuck-nonce, no dead ASIC domains, HW err% not climbing after settle. Prefer settings that hold for hours. Leave one notch of margin.

## Order
1. **Shared cooling first** — rack assist air, autofan on, temptarget 60, sane minFanSpeed floor.
2. **Undervolt ladder** — one notch at a time at fixed MHz; settle at least 15-20 min; pass if rej/domains/err/HR stay clean.
3. **On undervolt fail** — drop MHz one notch and retry the same lower vcore. Do not knee-jerk raise voltage first.
4. **When fans are lazy** — raise MHz one notch at current vcore; settle; fail then drop MHz keep vcore.
5. **Log every fail** into per-unit ledger + fleet-gotchas. Exclude that board from blanket pushes.

## Fan percent vs VR
Hex Gamma **fan % is ASIC chip PID chasing temptarget** — it does **not** see VR temperature. A VR-pad heatsink or pad work will not drop fan percent when the chip PID is still hot. Fan-vs-clock scatter across a fleet is mostly **TIM/paste, screw torque, and cooler flatness**, not silicon binning or small ambient swings. Fix heat-plate contact (or park clocks), not the wrong heatsink, when fans stay pinned.

## Post-restart error watermark
After a frequency/coreVoltage change that restarts the miner, **ignore the first errorPercentage sample** (boot / re-init noise). Judge the tune on the **settled** reading after the usual 15-20 min window (and any second sample). Do not roll back solely on the first post-boot err spike.

## Standing habits
- Confirm with the owner before PATCH on existing units (unless they just ordered that change).
- Never print pool passwords. Never send masked password stars back as a password.
- Hermetic water coolers: never suggest fluid top-off; levers are heat-plate/TIM, rack air, clocks.
- Cool morning shop is not OPP for MHz bumps; evening cool/lazy fans are the interesting headroom signal.
- Vcore/MHz often need restart for clean re-init; minFanSpeed can apply live.
- New Hex defaults (unless owner says otherwise): 525 MHz, autofan on, temptarget 60, displayTimeout 15.
- On ESP-Miner 2.15.3+, set fallback via pool slot id=1 PATCH; legacy fallback URL alone is ignored.

## Example gotcha shapes (illustrative — learn the owner's)
- Duplicate share + one ASIC about 2x peers means undervolt instability at that MHz/vcore.
- Soft HR + high HW err% with limp ASICs means too aggressive MHz at that vcore; drop MHz.
- Grab /api/system/logs before rollback when diagnosing.

routines.name: fleet health check
routines.description: Evening LAN poll of the ASIC inventory: totals, TROUBLE vs OPP flags, no auto clock changes.
routines.content:
Evening ASIC fleet health check from the owner's LAN computer.

Do not print pool passwords or keys. Do not nmap. Do not PATCH clocks or voltages unless the owner already ordered a change in chat.

From the fleet inventory, light ping + GET http://IP/api/system/info on each listed miner. Summarize reachable/total, wall watts, hashrate (TH), and approximate J/TH.

Flag TROUBLE for: down/timeout, not Connected, fans pinned near 100% for a long stretch, chip temp over about 65C, HW err% climbing or about 2%+, wifiRSSI -70 or worse (note wrong mesh node if -80 or worse), or miners stuck on fallback when primary should be up.

Flag OPP only when fans are cool/lazy in a warm shop evening (thermal headroom for a one-notch MHz bump). Never treat a cool morning as OPP. List OPP candidates; do not auto PATCH.

If a local pool UI / worker headcount is configured, prefer a quick pool headcount when the stats dashboard flickers before declaring a mass miner outage.

Append a one-line summary to the fleet health log if the owner set a path. Send the owner a short shop-floor note with the summary, TROUBLE, and OPP (or none). No Daily Tasks watches. No WiFi factory resets from this routine.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 4 18 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
